metadata.source: Compiled from individual institutions' own official admissions pages where verifiable (see 'source_url' per entry). Fields marked verified=false could not be confirmed against an official source in this pass and should be treated as unknown, not fact.
notes: The original file's 'General Science / Computing' program, its 85-91 mid-50 range, 80% cutoff, and 15/35/35/15 entering-grade distribution were identical templated placeholders across 36 institutions and were not real data. No Canadian university publishes a program called 'General Science / Computing'.

Most Ontario/Canadian universities do NOT use a fixed hard 'cutoff'; official policy (e.g. University of Waterloo) is that admission averages fluctuate year to year with applicant pool size and are not guaranteed by any specific number.

Where a university publishes an official university-wide minimum admission average (the real, sourceable equivalent of a 'cutoff'), that figure is used instead, with a citation. Note this floor is an ELIGIBILITY minimum, not the competitive average needed to actually get an offer -- competitive programs routinely admit well above it.

'cudo_entering_distribution' and per-program 'historical_mid_50_range' for generic programs have been removed for non-flagship entries because this granularity is not publicly published by these institutions and could not be verified; presenting invented numbers here would repeat the original problem.

The 5 named, real flagship programs (McGill CS, McMaster Health Sci, UofT EngSci, UofT CS, Waterloo SE/CS/SYDE) are kept because they correspond to actual programs with some publicly reportable data, but competitive averages there reflect self-reported ranges (e.g. Uniscope), not official published cutoffs, and are labeled accordingly.

2026-08-28 research pass: newly verified official minimums for Brock University (70%), Toronto Metropolitan University (70%), and Western University (80%). Western in particular publishes a much higher typical *entering* average (~88%) alongside its 80% eligibility floor; both figures are recorded separately below so they aren't conflated.

batch_2_research_notes.scope_requested: Computer Science, Engineering (general/Mechanical/Civil), Psychology/Life Sciences across all 41 institutions
batch_2_research_notes.honest_finding: Per-program numeric cutoffs are, with very few exceptions (McGill CS, McMaster Health Sci, UofT EngSci/CS, Waterloo SE/CS/SYDE -- already in your file), NOT officially published by Canadian universities for these program areas. Official pages almost universally state either (a) a university-wide minimum floor, or (b) that competitive averages vary by year/pool with no fixed number. Where a genuinely useful program-specific figure exists, it typically comes from Uniscope (a self-report aggregator), which is labeled as such below -- never presented as an official cutoff.
batch_2_research_notes.methodology: Each entry below was checked against the institution's own admissions/registrar site this session. Uniscope figures are cited separately and flagged as self-reported/unofficial.

updated_institutions.note: OUInfo (Ontario's official cross-university admissions info service, sourced from Windsor itself): 'All programs require a minimum admission average (typically 70%), which may change from year to year depending on the number of applicants and available seats.' This is a floor, not a competitive average -- no official per-program CS/Engineering/Psychology cutoff found.

Laurier's own site: 'If your admission average is below the minimum admission average required for your program (to a minimum of 70%)...' Science programs, BBA, and Economics factor required courses into the average; other programs use top-six 4U/M. No official fixed per-program CS/Engineering/Psychology cutoff published -- Laurier does not offer a general Engineering program (Physics/Computer Science are its closest STEM offerings).

U of A's own admissions pages: minimum general admission average of 70% on five required Grade 12-level subjects; individual faculties may require higher. U of A explicitly publishes rolling 'Competitive Requirements' trend data by faculty (not a fixed cutoff) at the source URL -- check that page directly for current-cycle Engineering/Science/Arts (Psychology) trend ranges, as it updates each cycle and pulling a static number here would go stale immediately.

Ontario Tech's own admissions policy states minimum requirements are normal minimums only and 'the specific average of standing required for admission varies from year-to-year'; no fixed university-wide number is codified in policy. However, sample offer letters published by the university (e.g. Bachelor of Commerce) consistently show 70% as the minimum final admissions average in practice. Treat 70% as strongly evidenced but not a hard published policy floor the way Carleton/Queen's/TMU/Dal state theirs.

programs_researched_no_official_cutoff_f.finding: No official CS-specific cutoff on uottawa.ca. General university minimum is 75% (OUInfo, official), with a note that 'many programs require a greater admission average.' A minimum combined 70% is required specifically in math/science prerequisite courses. Uniscope lists Computer Engineering (a related but distinct program) at ~86% competitive average / 46% acceptance rate -- self-reported, not official, and not the same program as CS.

York does not publish one university-wide minimum. Like Waterloo, it publishes per-program bands directly on each program's admissions page (examples found range from low-70s to high-80s depending on program). A per-program number would need to be pulled individually from each program's own futurestudents.yorku.ca page rather than a single site-wide figure.
